outputs.explanation: Panel A is a schematic (breast anatomy diagram) plus a classification table; it contains no plotted averaged data requiring individual points.
Panel B is a conceptual schematic depicting circadian phenotypes and study aims; no quantitative plot is present.
Panel C is a schematic illustrating the luciferase recording method; it shows no averaged data plot.

Panel D shows idealized/representative oscillation traces (Model #1-3) drawn purely to illustrate the stationary/non-stationary analysis workflow, not actual averaged experimental data — an illustrative curve within a schematic, not a data plot.
Panel E is a correlation heatmap; heatmaps are exempt from the individual-data-points requirement.
Panel F shows a schematic line-plot example (hypothetical 'Model 1/2/3' growth curves) used to illustrate the growth-rate quantification concept, not real averaged data with replicates.
Panel G shows an illustrative dose-response curve schematic used to explain the growth-rate-inhibition metric concept, not an actual averaged data plot.
Panel H contains an illustrative heatmap and a binary mutation table used as schematic examples of the genomic analysis workflow; heatmaps/tables are exempt and no real averaged bar data is shown.
Panel I contains scatter plots (PCA cluster plot and 3D circadian-parameter plot); scatter plots are exempt from the individual-data-points requirement since the points themselves are the data.
